solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pedal car has scored, entertaining 50 children!

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest within, so the word for scored takes in the Roman fifty

parts.note: to score is to cut a line into something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ch. is a standard abbreviation for child or children

explanation.surface: A child's pedal car has racked up points while hosting fifty youngsters at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedal car' looks like a toy, but the definition is the pedal a car has; 'entertaining' puts L inside CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Every manual car has a clutch pedal, worked by the left foot to change gear.

clue.text: Fail to nab limited parking space on vacation

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the last letter of the nab word goes

parts.note: to collar someone is to nab or arrest them
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters of space remain

explanation.surface: An attempt to grab a limited parking spot while on holiday goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims COLLAR to COLLA; 'on vacation' empties space to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to break down or fall through, a dramatic failure.

clue.text: Started down path

parts.note: under means below, the sense of down
a way is a path or route

explanation.surface: Someone set off along a path going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A project that is under way has begun and is in progress.

clue.text: Gloated about soldiers having won

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers
W is the symbol for the won, the currency of Korea

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about the troops' victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old past tense of crow, as in 'the cock crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or gloat, and its old past tense is the answer.

clue.text: Small staff with time aboard has ship immaculate

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the letter for time climbs onto the staff

parts.note: a staff is a pole or stick
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A small crew plus a punctual officer keep their vessel in perfect order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts T into POLE to give POTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immaculate has no stain or mark at all, which is the literal sense of being without spots.

clue.text: Guardian's following article announced in UN

indicators.note: following means the guardian's letters come after the article's
announced means spoken aloud, so the word for article is entered by its sound

parts.note: a piece is an article, as in a newspaper
a keeper is a guardian; the 's adds the plural letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper item states the Guardian's line on the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but is KEEPER. PIECE is spoken like the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: UN forces are known as peacekeepers, troops sent to maintain truces.

clue.text: Finest cover's a quilt made last century

parts.note: a top is a cover or lid; the 's is just a link

indicators.note: made means put together, so the letters of a quilt are reassembled
last points to the final letter of century

explanation.surface: The best bedspread is a quilt stitched in the last century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges A QUILT into QUALIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-quality goods are of the highest grade, the very best available.

clue.text: Greets migrating birds

indicators.note: migrating means moving away, so the letters of greets move into a new order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher welcomes flocks of birds on their seasonal journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: Policeman intercepts evil gang leader on railway track

indicators.note: intercepts means comes between, so the policeman's letters sit inside the evil word

parts.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing
DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of gang

explanation.surface: A detective catches an evil gang boss on the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short branch of railway track off the main line, used for parking trains.

clue.text: Tenant with large unruly dog's about to be rejected

indicators.note: unruly means out of order, so the letters of the dog are jumbled

parts.note: the dog supplies its three letters; the 's is just a link

indicators.note: rejected here means turned back, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A renter with a big unruly hound is about to be turned away by the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' turns DOG into ODG; 'to be rejected' flips RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger is a paying tenant who rents a room in someone else's home.

clue.text: Little girl sounded content to be made a fuss of

parts.note: Pam is a short form of the girl's name Pamela

indicators.note: sounded signals that a word heard spoken is to be entered by its sound

parts.note: a cat shows it is content by purring, so content gives the word purred

explanation.surface: A small girl made a happy noise when everyone fussed over her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' is a cat's happy purring; 'sounded' means only its sound counts, which suits the unstressed end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper someone is to indulge or spoil them with attention and comforts.

clue.text: Accounts supported by these sliding scales

indicators.note: in a down entry, being supported by means sitting on top, so the scales word comes first

parts.note: a balance is a pair of weighing scales

indicators.note: sliding means slipping out of place, so the letters of these are rearranged

explanation.surface: The figures are propped up by some unreliable weighing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' reads as a plural noun but gives the singular weighing device; in a down entry 'supported by' sets it on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance sheet is a statement of a company's assets and liabilities, part of its financial records.

clue.text: Champion's left raceway, crashing to one side

indicators.note: crashing suggests a smash-up, so the remaining track letters are thrown into a new order
left means has departed, so the champion's letters come out of the raceway

parts.note: an ace is a champion or star performer; the 's is short for has

explanation.surface: A racing champion has quit the track after a crash that sent the car veering off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes ACE out of RACEWAY, leaving RWAY; 'crashing' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or off-centre is turned to one side, out of its proper line.

clue.text: Writer's worried about America after January

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the writer is the answer

indicators.note: after means the January abbreviation comes first, followed by the rest
about means surrounding, so the worry word goes round America

parts.note: eaten can mean worried or troubled, as in 'what's eating you?'
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: An author frets about the United States as the new year begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym, as in being eaten up by worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist of Pride and Prejudice and Emma is one of the best-known English writers.

clue.text: Close northern pass including area around trailhead

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the northern letter and the pass word surround the rest

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters of area are rearranged

parts.note: read as head of trail, its first letter

explanation.surface: A northern mountain pass near a hiking trailhead is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb meaning shut, but it is the adjective meaning nearby; 'around' scrambles area.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by in place or time is within easy reach, nearby.

clue.text: Hamleys' criminal confronted, consumed with embarrassment

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the scrambled shop name takes in the word for confronted
criminal suggests something crooked, so the shop name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Hamleys is a famous London toy shop
to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: A crook at Hamleys toy shop is caught and challenged, burning with shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamleys is a large London toy store; its apostrophe is just surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting shamefacedly means showing guilt or embarrassment in one's manner.

clue.text: Sticky and hot taking tablets in a seedy bar

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the hot letter and tablets go within the bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

indicators.note: taking means adding on, so the tablets follow the hot letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: A sweaty clubber popping pills in a grimy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: E for an ecstasy tablet is a common crossword convention, made plural here.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive substance is one that sticks things together, such as glue.

clue.text: Make the most of saying one's leading event

parts.note: a maxim is a saying or proverb
one's is I'S, the Roman one plus is

indicators.note: leading points to the first letter of event

explanation.surface: An adage claims one person is the star of the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximise something is to increase it to its greatest extent, exploiting it fully.

clue.text: Crazy plan to take two drugs each on one day

indicators.note: on here means added after, so the each abbreviation is placed after the day letter

parts.note: crack (cocaine) and pot (cannabis) are two drugs
I is the Roman numeral for one
ea. is the abbreviation for each, as on price lists

explanation.surface: A mad scheme to take a couple of narcotics daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places EA after ID, reversing the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crank, so a crackpot idea is a wildly impractical scheme.

clue.text: Craft fair welcoming a fine fibre for weaving

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the jumbled fair surrounds the other letters
to craft is to fashion or shape, so the letters of fair are remade

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A craft fair features a good natural material for basketry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft fair' reads as an event; 'Craft' rearranges FAIR to RFIA, with AF inserted after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm-leaf fibre used for weaving baskets and mats.

clue.text: American city rents about to rise out of control

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the city and rents letters are read backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
rents are rips or tears

explanation.surface: Rents in a US city are about to soar uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rents' looks like housing costs but means tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that spiral climb ever faster in an uncontrolled upward curve.

clue.text: For starters, papers mistaken about revolutionary plot

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled papers go round the reversed plot
mistaken means wrongly ordered, so the letters of papers are rearranged
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for plot is read backwards

parts.note: a plot of land is a site

explanation.surface: To begin with, the newspapers got the story of a rebel conspiracy wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For starters' looks like 'first of all' but is the definition. 'mistaken' makes APPERS; 'revolutionary' gives ETIS, placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetisers are small dishes served at the start of a meal, which diners call starters.

clue.text: Made linguine sample for posh grocery

indicators.note: a sample is a small piece taken from within, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone made fresh pasta to offer as a taster in an upmarket food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across maDE LInguine.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling fine, often imported foods, an upmarket kind of grocer.

clue.text: Greatness of Velázquez isn't part of retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gallery's look back at the Spanish painter fails to convey his greatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness can mean magnitude or bulk, the physical extent of a thing.

clue.text: Sailors gulped drink after Field Officer ditched

indicators.note: after means the officer's letters lead and the rest follows
gulped means swallowed, so the sailors' letters take in the drink

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Navy men downed a drink after an officer abandoned them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditched' sits at the end like part of the story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means abandoned or deserted, just as something ditched has been dropped.

clue.text: British family wearing team's beachwear

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the family sits inside the team's letters

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, written as two ones, II
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A British clan sport the team's swimming costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven is written 11, read as the two letters II.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit, typical clothing for the beach.

clue.text: Mention mishandled duel in a low voice

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled duel sits within the singing voice

parts.note: alto is a low voice, the lowest female singing range

indicators.note: mishandled means badly managed, so the letters of duel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs a reference to a botched duel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a low voice' suggests whispering, but it is the singing range alto.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to refer to something indirectly, a passing mention.

clue.text: Admire an American hero

definitions.meaning: to hold someone in deep respect or awe
Paul ..., the patriot famed for his midnight ride warning of British troops in 1775

explanation.surface: Look up to a hero of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Revering is profound admiration, and Paul Revere is a celebrated American Revolutionary figure.
